title: Build Orders
blurb: Six workflows the exam expects you to replay from memory — click each step into the only order that ships.

ladders.title: How a generative model produces text
ladders.prompt: Put the steps in the order a generative model turns your prompt into text.

steps.label: Tokenization
steps.detail: Input text is split into tokens — words or sub-words — each mapped to an id from the model's vocabulary; nothing downstream has meaning until this happens (Task 1.2).

steps.label: Embeddings
steps.detail: Each token id is converted into a numeric vector encoding meaning — the same vector space that makes semantic similarity computable as vector distance.

steps.label: Transformer attention
steps.detail: Self-attention layers weigh every token against every other token in the sequence — the mechanic that 'powers most modern foundation models,' and it needs the embedding vectors to already exist.

steps.label: Next-token prediction
steps.detail: The model outputs a probability distribution over the whole vocabulary for the single next token; temperature and top-p reshape this distribution before one token is sampled.

steps.label: Detokenized output
steps.detail: The predicted token id is decoded back to text and the loop repeats one token at a time until a stop condition — perplexity measures how well this step's predictions matched held-out text.

ladders.title: Chat client with the Foundry SDK
ladders.prompt: Put the code flow in the order it must run.

steps.label: Install azure-ai-projects
steps.detail: 'Which package should you install for the project client?' is a classic exam stem — the answer is azure-ai-projects.

steps.label: Create AIProjectClient(endpoint, DefaultAzureCredential())
steps.detail: Endpoint + credential must both exist before any call; keyless auth = Entra ID DefaultAzureCredential.

steps.label: Call get_openai_client()
steps.detail: Bridges the project client to an OpenAI-compatible chat client — the line that breaks everything if removed.

steps.label: Build the messages list (system prompt first, then user prompt)
steps.detail: Rules and guardrails in the system message; this turn's request in the user message.

steps.label: Call chat.completions.create(model=DEPLOYMENT_NAME, messages=[...])
steps.detail: model= takes YOUR deployment name, never the base model name — the classic trap.

steps.label: Read response.choices[0].message.content
steps.detail: The reply text lives on the first choice's message — corpus snippet questions end here.

ladders.title: Agent lifecycle
ladders.prompt: Put the agent's lifecycle in the order it must happen.

steps.label: Define the agent: PromptAgentDefinition(model=MODEL_NAME, instructions=..., tools=[...])
steps.detail: Model + instructions + tools set at definition time — {"deployment":{"model":AGENT_NAME}} is the canonical wrong answer; deployments host models, agents are model + instructions + tools.

steps.label: Test it in the Agents playground
steps.detail: The playground configures persona, tools, and attached knowledge side by side and lets you try multi-turn behavior before any client code calls the agent.

steps.label: Save it: project.agents.create_version(agent_name=AGENT_NAME, definition=...)
steps.detail: Unsaved playground edits are lost on leaving the portal — create_version is what actually persists a definition, whether you built it in the portal or in code.

steps.label: Create a thread: openai.conversations.create()
steps.detail: Opens the runtime container that later turns write into — called by the client app before the first message is sent, distinct from the agent's own definition.

steps.label: Add the user's message to the thread
steps.detail: The turn's content is appended to the thread's accumulating message history — a run can't process a message that hasn't been added yet.

steps.label: Create a run and read the output: openai.responses.create(..., extra_body={"agent_reference": {...}})
steps.detail: The invocation that actually processes the conversation and produces the agent's next output; agent_reference is per-call metadata pointing at the saved definition.

ladders.title: Speech SDK call order
ladders.prompt: Put the Speech SDK calls in the order they must run.

steps.label: SpeechConfig(subscription=key, region=region)
steps.detail: Every Speech SDK flow starts here — the key/region (or endpoint) pair that authenticates every call that follows.

steps.label: Set speech_config.speech_synthesis_voice_name = "..."
steps.detail: Voice selection is a property set directly on the config object — exam's DragonHD-voice snippet sets this line right after SpeechConfig, before any other object is built from it.

steps.label: AudioConfig(...) — microphone, file, or default device
steps.detail: Built independently of the voice-name property, but quickstart snippets construct it only after config setup is finished, immediately before the recognizer/synthesizer that will consume both objects.

steps.label: Create the Recognizer or Synthesizer: SpeechRecognizer(speech_config, audio_config) / SpeechSynthesizer(speech_config)
steps.detail: Both constructors take the already-built speech_config (the recognizer also takes audio_config) — nothing after this point can still inject the config.

steps.label: Call recognize_once() / speak_text_async(text)
steps.detail: recognize_once() captures one short utterance (vs. continuous recognition); speak_text_async() actually plays the text — the async future/.get() pattern belongs here, last, once the object exists.

ladders.title: Classic voice pipeline
ladders.prompt: Put the classic voice-agent pipeline in order.

steps.label: Speech-to-text: convert the caller's spoken audio into text
steps.detail: Pipeline step one — recognize_once() or continuous recognition turns audio into a transcript before any reasoning can happen on it.

steps.label: Language / generative-AI processing: reason over the transcript and produce a text reply
steps.detail: A chat/agent call reasons over the transcript — the step a single multimodal model (e.g. audio-in/audio-out chat deployment) can collapse together with steps 1 and 3, and the one the Voice Live API is built to replace all three of at once with a single low-latency speech-to-speech interface.

steps.label: Text-to-speech: synthesize the reply back to audio
steps.detail: speak_text_async() plays the generated reply — the classic pipeline's final step, also foldable into the single-multimodal-model or Voice Live alternative named in step 2's detail.

ladders.title: Content Understanding workflow
ladders.prompt: Put the Content Understanding workflow in order.

steps.label: Choose or define an analyzer: describe the schema in natural language (ContentAnalyzer(base_analyzer_id=..., field_schema=...))
steps.detail: Prebuilt analyzer ids (prebuilt-invoice, prebuilt-audio,...) cover common domains; a custom ContentAnalyzer names the fields you want in plain language via field_schema — no code beyond describing what to extract.

steps.label: Register it: client.begin_create_analyzer(...)
steps.detail: Provisions the analyzer definition as a long-running operation before it can be called against any content — a one-time setup step, not a per-document one.

steps.label: Submit content: client.begin_analyze(analyzer_id=..., inputs=[AnalysisInput(url=file_url)])
steps.detail: Each document/image/audio/video file gets its own begin_analyze call against the already-registered analyzer — the per-document step, unlike step 2.

steps.label: Poll the operation: poller.result()
steps.detail: begin_analyze returns a poller; call its.result() method to wait for the final analysis output — analysis is asynchronous, not a synchronous return (the exam calls it 'call the poller's ________ method').

steps.label: Read the structured JSON fields from the result
steps.detail: The extracted fields — vendor name, invoice date, invoice total, and the like — land in the poller's result payload; this is where Content Understanding's own job ends.

steps.label: Hand off to Azure AI Search for indexing
steps.detail: Content Understanding only extracts — it never indexes or generates; Azure AI Search is the separate downstream service that indexes CU's structured output for retrieval/RAG.
